rv.q: And even if the laughs come more readily than the tears, perhaps it's for the best that PrideArts's A NEW BRAIN serves as a welcome prescription for joy at a time when many of us may feel lost in the gloomiest of swamps.

To craft a hilarious and touching musical out of a subject as unfunny and serious as arteriovenous malformation and brain surgery is a formidable challenge and Finn and Lapine succeed beyond any expectations.
A New Brain serves up equal parts midlife crisis and joyous queer representation on stage.
While not considered William Finn’s finest work, this musical offers an often entertaining look at the creative mind.

As I was saying (before I so rudely interrupted myself), though the play itself was not, IMHO, worthy of the creator of Into the Woods , the production was top-notch and totally worthy of the occasion.
It’s very much a feel-good production, too, and a good way to kick off the 2025-2026 theater season.
What’s so wonderful about this production is the brilliant directing by Jay Españo!
If you like feel-good musicals that embrace silliness and have a positive message at the end, A New Brain would be a good show for you.

cn.t: Critics praise this lively, charming production of William Finn's autobiographical musical, highlighting Jay Españo's brilliant direction, the bouncing jazz-inflected score, and joyous queer representation delivered with creativity and heart.
